_comment: Differences that already existed before the editor refactor started.
They are reported separately and do not fail the audit, so that a NEW
difference introduced by the refactor is never buried in old noise.
Every entry is a real finding and gets closed as its section is rebuilt.
Nothing goes in here to make the audit quiet.

missing_in_editor.left_panel_cards: Managed by _renderPanelCardList, a dedicated YAML card list rather than a field. Not missing, just not a picker -- listed so the audit stays quiet without pretending it checked it.
missing_in_editor.temp_indoor_entity: Top-level legacy fallback read alongside entities.temp_*. The entities.* form is what the editor offers and what the card prefers; these remain readable so old YAML keeps working. Clean-up candidate for when the climate section is rebuilt.
missing_in_editor.temp_outdoor_entity: Top-level legacy fallback read alongside entities.temp_*. The entities.* form is what the editor offers and what the card prefers; these remain readable so old YAML keeps working. Clean-up candidate for when the climate section is rebuilt.
missing_in_editor.temp_forecast_high_entity: Top-level legacy fallback read alongside entities.temp_*. The entities.* form is what the editor offers and what the card prefers; these remain readable so old YAML keeps working. Clean-up candidate for when the climate section is rebuilt.
missing_in_editor.temp_forecast_low_entity: Top-level legacy fallback read alongside entities.temp_*. The entities.* form is what the editor offers and what the card prefers; these remain readable so old YAML keeps working. Clean-up candidate for when the climate section is rebuilt.

surplus_in_editor.venus_charge: Offered as a sensor picker, but the renderer only names it in the top-level-to-entities migration list -- no code path displays it. The battery bubble's equivalents (battery_charge / battery_discharge) ARE read, so this is an inconsistency in the CARD, not the editor. Kept visible rather than silently removed: a user may have one configured. Needs a decision -- wire it up in the renderer, or drop both controls.
